title: Cylindrical base
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a single face. Within this face, draw a single loop and within this loop, draw a circle centered at coordinates [0.0225, 0.0225] with a radius of 0.0225 units. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.045. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using Euler angles of zero degrees and translating it using a vector of zero. Finally, extrude the two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units to create a solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical base will be 0.045 units in length, 0.045 units in width, and 0.75 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circle in the sketch
r = r.center(0.0225, 0.0225).circle(0.0225)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Scale the sketch (this step is not necessary as the scale is applied to the sketch, not the final extrusion)
# r = r.scale(0.045)  # This line is commented out because scaling after extrusion does not make sense

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0225, 0.0225)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0225)  # Draw the circle with the specified radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
